docs.title: Welcome
docs.text:
Any-to-Any Terminology Mapping is an open-source Python framework designed to facilitate terminology mapping tasks. The library organizes this process in a modular and extensible way to support multiple use cases and incorporate new techniques as they emerge.

In simple terms, mapping a new expression to a specific terminology involves considering many possible expressions, retrieving the best candidate target terms, and selecting them manually, which can be effortful and time-consuming.

AATM leverages the OMOP vocabularies to facilitate this task. These vocabularies reflect large, community-driven mapping efforts that connect many different health-related terminologies and classifications worldwide and organize them around standard terminologies, which serve as the central connecting nodes in the system. As these mapping efforts continue, healthcare-related concepts become increasingly well represented in these vocabularies, creating a virtuous cycle and increasing the chances of finding a strong correspondence for a new unmapped expression.

Standard vocabularies

To accomplish this, AATM organizes the mapping process into very simple steps:

  • translation, which can be optional;
  • retrieval, which explores what is available from prior mapping efforts; and
  • selection, which connects a standard concept to the new expression being mapped.

Once this connection is made, every link associated with that standard concept becomes immediately available, enabling mapping to many different terminologies and classifications that are already connected to that concept, effectively breaking down barriers to interoperability in healthcare.

Terminology mapping pipeline

AATM also includes an information extraction pipeline that finds entities such as conditions, drugs and their dates in clinical documents with an LLM, and validates every extracted span against the source text. The extracted expressions can then be mapped with the terminology mapping pipeline. See the Information extraction quick start.

docs.title: Design principles
docs.text:
Modularity

AATM is designed as a pipeline of clearly separated components, each responsible for a specific part of the terminology mapping process. Translation, retrieval, reranking, and selection are treated as independent steps with well-defined interfaces. This separation makes the library easier to understand, test, maintain, and adapt. It also allows users to inspect and improve one part of the workflow without having to redesign the entire system.

This modular structure is especially important because terminology mapping is not a single uniform problem. Different use cases may require different translation strategies, retrieval methods, or selection criteria depending on the source language, target terminology, domain, or level of ambiguity in the input expressions. By isolating responsibilities, AATM allows each part of the pipeline to evolve independently while remaining compatible with the broader framework.

Extensibility

AATM was built with the expectation that terminology mapping methods will continue to evolve. New embedding models, retrieval systems, rerankers, large language model–based selectors, rule-based selectors, and domain-specific heuristics can be incorporated into the framework without requiring major changes to its core design. Users can replace existing components or add new ones while preserving the overall pipeline structure.

This extensibility is important both for research and for production settings. In research, it enables rapid experimentation with new methods and easier comparison between approaches. In applied settings, it allows users to adapt the system to new terminologies, new languages, and new operational requirements. In this sense, AATM is intended not only as a tool for performing terminology mapping, but also as a flexible foundation for building and evaluating new mapping workflows.

Simplicity

Although terminology mapping can involve complex methods, AATM is designed to keep the overall process conceptually simple. The framework reduces the task to a small number of intuitive steps that reflect how a person might approach the problem: optionally translate the input, retrieve possible matches, rerank or organize the candidates, and select the best concept. This organization helps make the library more accessible to users who are not specialists in information retrieval or machine learning.

Simplicity also guides the user experience. The library aims to provide clear abstractions, predictable behavior, and straightforward ways to configure and run mapping pipelines. This makes it easier to get started with basic workflows while still leaving room for more advanced customization when needed. By prioritizing simplicity, AATM seeks to lower the barrier to terminology mapping and make interoperable healthcare data workflows more approachable.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
Welcome to AATM — the Any-to-Any Terminology Mapper.

AATM helps you map source terminology expressions to standardized concepts through a modular pipeline composed of:

  • translation
  • retrieval
  • reranking
  • selection

It is designed so you can start simple and progressively swap components as needed.

docs.title: What AATM does
docs.text:
At a high level, AATM takes source concepts such as:

  • local clinical terms
  • source vocabulary descriptions
  • free-text expressions

and maps them to standardized concepts using a pipeline like this:

source concept
  -> translator
  -> retriever
  -> reranker
  -> selector
  -> mapped concept

The default workflow is centered on OMOP-style terminology mapping.

docs.title: Information extraction
docs.text:
AATM can also extract structured information from clinical documents, such as conditions, drugs, dates and routes, before it is mapped:

clinical note
  -> numbered lines
  -> LLM extraction (guided by entity definitions)
  -> validation against the note
  -> validated entities and records

See the Information extraction quick start, and Writing entity definitions to describe your own entities in YAML.

docs.title: Project artifacts created locally
docs.text:
AATM uses a local .aatm/ directory to store generated assets such as:

.aatm/
├── omop.db
├── datasets/
└── chroma_vector_dbs/

Typical outputs are written to:

output/

docs.title: TerminologyMapper
docs.text:
TerminologyMapper is the main orchestration class of AATM.

It coordinates the full mapping workflow by combining the pipeline components into an end-to-end process. In practice, it is responsible for:

  • loading source concepts from an input file
  • optionally translating source descriptions
  • retrieving candidate standard concepts
  • optionally reranking retrieved results
  • selecting the final mapped concept
  • returning the results as a DataFrame
  • writing the mapped output to disk

It is the main entry point when you want to run terminology mapping in batch mode.

Typical usage:

from aatm.terminology_mapper import TerminologyMapper
from aatm.registries.translators import load_translator
from aatm.registries.retrievers import load_retriever
from aatm.registries.rerankers import load_reranker
from aatm.registries.selectors import load_selector

mapper = TerminologyMapper(
    translator=load_translator("empty-translator"),
    retriever=load_retriever("embeddinggemma-300M"),
    reranker=load_reranker("bm25-reranker"),
    selector=load_selector("first-result-selector"),
    batch_size=100,
)

results_df = mapper.map("source_to_concept_map.csv")

docs.title: Translator
docs.text:
Translators convert input text into English before retrieval.

Examples:

  • EmptyTranslator
  • GeminiTranslator
  • OpenAITranslator

Use EmptyTranslator when your inputs are already in the desired language.

docs.title: Retriever
docs.text:
Retrievers fetch candidate concepts from a vector database.

Main implementation:

  • ChromaDBRetriever

docs.title: Reranker
docs.text:
Rerankers reorder retrieved candidates.

Examples:

  • BM25Reranker
  • Qwen3Reranker

docs.title: Selector
docs.text:
Selectors choose the final mapped concept from the retrieved candidates.

Examples:

  • FirstResultSelector
  • OpenAILLMSelector
  • GeminiLLMSelector

docs.title: Information extraction
docs.text:
The extraction pipeline turns clinical text into structured entities that can later be mapped.

  • Entity definitions (EntityDefinitions) describe what to extract. They are loaded from YAML, either predefined (condition_occurrence, drug_exposure, ecog_performance_status, lab_results, smoking_status, family_history, medical_history, device_exposure) or your own. An entity can require a parent, such as a start date that belongs to a condition, and can define attributes: labels from a fixed list assigned to each mention, such as the result of a test. See Writing entity definitions.
  • Extractor (SimpleLLMExtractor) sends each document to an LLM as numbered lines. The model returns each mention with an id, its exact text, its line and the ids of its parents.
  • Validation (validate_extracted_entity) keeps only mentions that exist on the given line, checks keys, parent links and attribute labels, and records why every rejected mention failed. A wrong label on an optional attribute is reported without dropping the mention.
  • Records (EntityValidationResult.to_records()) nest validated entities under their parents, ready to become table rows.

See the Information extraction quick start.

docs.title: Writing Entity Definitions
docs.text:
Entity definitions tell the extractor what to find in a clinical note. They live in a YAML file that you write once and reuse for every note. This page explains every field, how to choose between them, and how to load and check a file before spending any model calls.

If you have not run an extraction yet, start with the Information extraction quick start.

docs.title: A complete example
docs.text:
Suppose you want every BRCA test mentioned in oncology notes, when it was done, and what the result was:

brca.yaml
# BRCA testing in oncology notes.

- name: BRCA gene test
  key: brca_test
  definition: >
    A mention of BRCA1 and/or BRCA2 genetic testing performed for the patient,
    e.g. "BRCA1/2 panel" or "germline BRCA testing". Does not include tests of
    relatives or tests that are only planned.
  attributes:
    - key: result
      description: The result of the test as stated in the note.
      labels:
        - value: positive
          description: A pathogenic or likely pathogenic variant was reported.
        - value: negative
          description: No pathogenic or likely pathogenic variant was found.
        - value: uncertain
          description: Only a variant of uncertain significance (VUS) was reported.
    - key: origin
      description: Whether germline or tumour (somatic) DNA was tested.
      labels:
        - value: germline
          description: Germline testing, e.g. blood or saliva.
        - value: somatic
          description: Testing of tumour tissue.

- name: Test date
  definition: The date a BRCA test was performed or reported, e.g. "2024" or "March 2025".
  has_parent: true
  parent_key: brca_test

This file uses the three building blocks:

Building block In the example Answers Entity brca_test Where in the note is this mentioned? (an exact span) Parent link test_date → brca_test Which mention does this detail belong to? (another span) Attribute result, origin What does the note say about this mention? (a label from a fixed list)

Use it like any other definition file:

from aatm.data_models.extractors import EntityDefinitions
from aatm.extractors import SimpleLLMExtractor

entity_definitions = EntityDefinitions.from_yaml("brca.yaml")

extractor = SimpleLLMExtractor(model_id="openai/gpt-5", entity_definitions=entity_definitions)

note = "Germline BRCA1/2 panel 2024: no pathogenic variants detected."
(result,) = await extractor([note])

for record in result.to_records():
    dates = [d.text for d in record.children.get("test_date", [])]
    print(record.text, record.attributes, dates)

A typical answer:

Germline BRCA1/2 panel {'result': 'negative', 'origin': 'germline'} ['2024']

docs.title: Field reference
docs.text: A definition file is a YAML list. Each item is one entity.

docs.title: Entity fields
docs.text: Field Required Default Meaning name yes Human-readable name, shown to the model key no generated from name Identifier used in the model output and in your results. Lowercase letters, digits and _ only definition yes What counts as a mention. The model reads this, so it decides quality has_parent no false Every mention must be linked to a mention of parent_key parent_key when has_parent is true Key of the parent entity attributes no none Classifications the model assigns to each mention (see below) omop no none How each mention becomes a row of an OMOP CDM table. Never sent to the model. See From notes to OMOP tables

docs.title: Attribute fields
docs.text: Field Required Default Meaning key yes Identifier, unique within the entity. Lowercase letters, digits and _ only description yes What the attribute describes. The model reads it required no false Reject mentions that have no valid label for this attribute labels yes The allowed values, at least one

docs.title: Label fields
docs.text: Field Required Meaning value yes The label the model returns and you get back, e.g. negative. Unique within the attribute, ignoring case description yes When this label applies. The model reads it

docs.title: Keys
docs.text:
Keys are how entities refer to each other (parent_key) and how you find them in the results (entity.key, record.children["test_date"]).

  • Entity keys are optional. When omitted, the key is generated from the name: lowercase, accents removed, any other character replaced by _. "Test date" becomes test_date, "Condição — Início" becomes condicao_inicio.

  • When you set a key yourself, it must use lowercase letters, digits and single underscores between them (brca_test), the same form the generated keys have, because the model must return keys in this form. Anything else (BRCA-Test, brca__test, _brca) fails when the file is loaded, with a suggested key:

    Value error, Entity key 'BRCA-Test' must use only lowercase letters, digits and single underscores between them. Use 'brca_test' instead.

  • Attribute keys are always written by you and follow the same rule.

  • Keys must be unique: entity keys within the file, attribute keys within their entity.

Set the key explicitly when other entities refer to it as parent_key. Renaming the entity then cannot break the links.

docs.title: Parents: details that belong to a mention
docs.text:
Use a parent link when a piece of information only makes sense attached to another mention: a start date of a condition, the dose of a drug, the unit of a dose.

- name: Drug name
  key: drug_name
  definition: The name of a drug used by the patient, e.g. "Aspirin".

- name: Dose
  key: dose
  definition: The amount of one administration of a drug, e.g. "40".
  has_parent: true
  parent_key: drug_name

- name: Dose unit
  key: dose_unit
  definition: The unit of a dose, e.g. "mg".
  has_parent: true
  parent_key: dose
  • The child is a span too: it must appear on a line of the note, and you get its exact position.
  • Every mention of a child must name at least one parent mention. A child without a parent is rejected (required_parent_missing), and so is a child whose parent was rejected (parent_rejected).
  • One child mention can have several parents, e.g. one date that applies to two conditions.
  • Hierarchies can be any depth (drug → dose → unit), but not circular.

docs.title: Attributes: what the note says about a mention
docs.text:
Use an attribute when you need a judgement from a fixed list, not a piece of text: a test result, whether a condition is present or denied, whether it is the patient's or a relative's, whether a drug is current or past.

The label does not have to appear in the note. The model reads "no pathogenic variants detected" and answers negative.

docs.title: Attribute or child entity?
docs.text:
You want... Use Example The text itself, with its position A child entity The date "2024", the dose "40 mg" One of a fixed set of values An attribute result: negative Both: a fixed value and the text that justifies it An attribute on a child entity A brca_result child with span "no pathogenic variants detected" and attribute result: negative

The last pattern is useful when someone will audit the data: the label points at the exact words it was based on.

docs.title: Optional or required?
docs.text:
Optional (the default) is the right choice almost always. When the note does not state the attribute, the model leaves it out and the mention is kept without it. The model is told never to guess, so "the note does not say" and a real answer stay distinct. For BRCA, this keeps a VUS (uncertain, a real result) apart from a note that never gives the result (no result at all).

You do not need a not_stated or unknown label: a missing attribute already means that.

required: true means a mention is useless to you without the attribute. Mentions without a valid label are rejected, together with their children. Use it only when you would discard those mentions anyway, for example when you only want tests with a known result.

docs.title: Writing labels
docs.text:
• Describe every label, including the borderline cases. The descriptions are where you decide whether a VUS counts as uncertain or negative, or whether "possible pneumonia" is present or possible.
  • Make labels mutually exclusive: the model picks one per attribute.
  • Cover the cases you expect. A value that is not in the list is dropped and reported as invalid_label, so many such issues on one attribute suggest a missing label or an unclear description.
  • Keep values short and stable (positive, not Positive result reported). You will filter and count by them.

docs.title: How the model's labels are checked
docs.text:
Labels are checked after the model answers, against the file:

  • Case and surrounding spaces are ignored. If the model answers " Negative ", it is accepted as negative and stored exactly as you defined it, without any issue.
  • A wrong label on an optional attribute never drops the mention. The attribute is removed and the problem is reported, with the attribute key, so you can see which attribute causes trouble.
  • Attributes are checked only for mentions that pass every other check. A mention rejected for its text, line or parent adds no attribute issues, so the issue counts cover only mentions that were really found.
  • Duplicates: when the same mention is extracted twice, the first one's labels are kept. A label the first mention lacks is copied from the duplicate, a different label is reported as conflicting_duplicate, and a duplicate that is missing a required attribute is not reported, since the kept mention already has it.

See Attribute issues for the full list of issue reasons and how to count them.

docs.title: Writing good definitions
docs.text:
The definition and description fields are the prompt. Most extraction problems are fixed here.

  • Say what counts, with examples. e.g. "BRCA1/2 panel" or "germline BRCA testing".
  • Say what does not count. Tests of relatives, planned tests, negated findings, family history. The model includes them unless told otherwise.
  • Say how much text to take. "The name and dose form of a drug, e.g. "Aspirin 81 mg oral tablet"" gives longer spans than "The name of a drug".
  • One idea per entity. Split "condition and its severity" into an entity and an attribute (or a child entity).
  • Iterate on real notes. Look at unmatched_entities, unmatched_keys and the attribute issues after a few notes, and adjust the wording.

docs.title: YAML pitfalls
docs.text:
YAML converts some unquoted words, which then fail validation when the file is loaded:

Written YAML reads it as Write instead value: yes / no / on / off true / false value: "yes" value: true / false a boolean value: "true" value: null / ~ nothing value: "null" value: 1 / 2.5 a number value: "1" definition: Result: negative invalid YAML (second :) quote the text, or use >

For long text, use a folded block (>): lines are joined with spaces, and the trailing newline is removed when loaded.

  definition: >
    A mention of BRCA1 and/or BRCA2 genetic testing performed for the patient.
    Does not include tests of relatives.

Comments start with # and are ignored, which makes them a good place to explain choices to the next developer.

docs.title: Checking a file before using it
Load errors
docs.text:
Invalid files fail when loaded, before any model call, with a message that names the file:

  • an entity or attribute key that is not lowercase snake_case
  • duplicate entity keys, or duplicate attribute keys in one entity
  • has_parent: true without parent_key, or the reverse
  • a parent_key that does not exist, an entity that is its own parent, or a loop such as a -> b -> a
  • an attribute without labels, or two labels that differ only in case
  • a missing name, definition, description or label value, or a value of the wrong type (see YAML pitfalls)
ValueError: Invalid entity definitions in brca.yaml:
1 validation error for EntityDefinitions
entities.0.attributes.0.labels.0.value
  Input should be a valid string [type=string_type, input_value=True, input_type=bool]

The location (entities.0.attributes.0.labels.0.value) counts from 0: the first entity, its first attribute, its first label.

docs.title: See what the model will read
docs.text:
print(entity_definitions.to_prompt_str())

BRCA gene test (key: `brca_test`, has_parent: False, parent_key: `None`): A mention of BRCA1 and/or BRCA2 genetic testing performed for the patient, e.g. "BRCA1/2 panel" or "germline BRCA testing". Does not include tests of relatives or tests that are only planned.
  Attributes:
  - `result` (optional): The result of the test as stated in the note.
    - `positive`: A pathogenic or likely pathogenic variant was reported.
    - `negative`: No pathogenic or likely pathogenic variant was found.
    - `uncertain`: Only a variant of uncertain significance (VUS) was reported.
  - `origin` (optional): Whether germline or tumour (somatic) DNA was tested.
    - `germline`: Germline testing, e.g. blood or saliva.
    - `somatic`: Testing of tumour tissue.
Test date (key: `test_date`, has_parent: True, parent_key: `brca_test`): The date a BRCA test was performed or reported, e.g. "2024" or "March 2025".

If this text would confuse a colleague, it will confuse the model too.

docs.title: Test it without a model
docs.text:
validate_extracted_entity checks a hand-written answer against your definitions, so you can try edge cases in a unit test:

from aatm.data_models.extractors import ExtractedEntityCandidates, validate_extracted_entity

note = "BRCA1/2 panel 2024: no pathogenic variants detected."
candidates = ExtractedEntityCandidates.model_validate(
    {
        "entities": [
            {
                "id": "e1", "text": "BRCA1/2 panel", "key": "brca_test", "line": "L1",
                "attributes": [{"key": "result", "value": "negative"}],
            },
            {"id": "e2", "text": "2024", "key": "test_date", "line": "L1", "parents": ["e1"]},
        ]
    }
)
result = validate_extracted_entity(note, entity_definitions, candidates)
assert result.validated_entities[0].get_attribute("result") == "negative"

docs.title: Other ways to get definitions
docs.text:
Predefined files ship with AATM, aligned with OMOP CDM tables and common clinical scales. Their source in aatm/omop/entity_definitions/ is a good starting point to copy:

EntityDefinitions.from_predefined("condition_occurrence")
EntityDefinitions.from_predefined("drug_exposure")
EntityDefinitions.from_predefined("ecog_performance_status")
EntityDefinitions.from_predefined("lab_results")
EntityDefinitions.from_predefined("smoking_status")
EntityDefinitions.from_predefined("family_history")
EntityDefinitions.from_predefined("medical_history")
EntityDefinitions.from_predefined("device_exposure")

In Python, the same fields are available as models, which is handy for tests or definitions built at run time:

from aatm.data_models.extractors import (
    AttributeDefinition,
    AttributeLabel,
    EntityDefinition,
    EntityDefinitions,
)

entity_definitions = EntityDefinitions(
    entities=[
        EntityDefinition(
            name="BRCA gene test",
            key="brca_test",
            definition="A mention of BRCA1 and/or BRCA2 genetic testing.",
            attributes=[
                AttributeDefinition(
                    key="result",
                    description="The result of the test as stated in the note.",
                    labels=[
                        AttributeLabel(value="positive", description="A pathogenic variant was reported."),
                        AttributeLabel(value="negative", description="No pathogenic variant was found."),
                        AttributeLabel(value="uncertain", description="Only a VUS was reported."),
                    ],
                )
            ],
        ),
        EntityDefinition(
            name="Test date",
            definition="The date a BRCA test was performed.",
            has_parent=True,
            parent_key="brca_test",
        ),
    ]
)

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Some components depend on external APIs. Create a .env file in your project root when needed.

Example:

GOOGLE_API_KEY=your_google_api_key
OPENAI_API_KEY=your_openai_api_key
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=your_anthropic_api_key
OPENROUTER_API_KEY=your_openrouter_api_key

AATM loads environment variables automatically with python-dotenv.

The information extraction pipeline needs the key of the provider you use: OPENAI_API_KEY, GOOGLE_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or OPENROUTER_API_KEY. Local OpenAI-compatible servers such as Ollama usually need none. OPENAI_API_KEY and GOOGLE_API_KEY are also used by the OpenAI- and Gemini-based mapping components.

docs.title: Optional settings
docs.text: Variable Default Purpose AATM_LOG_LEVEL INFO Log level used by the CLI, the API and the search UI: DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR or CRITICAL. Same as the CLI option --log-level. STREAMLIT_SERVER_FILE_WATCHER_TYPE unset (watcher off) aatm search-ui disables Streamlit's file watcher unless this is set, e.g. to auto while editing the search UI.

docs.title: Logging in Python code
docs.text:
Importing aatm does not print anything. To see AATM's log messages in a notebook or script:

import logging
import aatm

aatm.configure_logging()               # INFO and above, on stderr
aatm.configure_logging(logging.DEBUG)  # everything
logging.getLogger("aatm.data_models.extractors").setLevel(logging.DEBUG)  # one module only

docs.title: Device selection
docs.text:
Variable Values Effect AATM_DEVICE cuda, mps, cpu Forces the device local models run on. If unset, AATM uses CUDA, then MPS, then CPU, whichever PyTorch can see first. AATM raises an error if the requested device is not available.

At INFO level, AATM logs the device local models run on (see the logging settings above).

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
The recommended way to install AATM is with uv, which also picks the right PyTorch build for your hardware (CUDA, Apple GPU or CPU) in a single command:

uv pip install aatm --torch-backend=auto

--torch-backend is a preview feature of uv. If it does not work for you, use pip as shown below.

With pip:

pip install aatm
aatm doctor

aatm doctor checks whether local models can use your GPU and, if not, prints the exact commands to fix it. See GPU acceleration below.

If you want to build from the source, clone the repository and install it locally:

pipuv 
git clone https://github.com/precisiondata/aatm.git
pip install -e . 

git clone https://github.com/precisiondata/aatm.git
uv sync

docs.title: GPU acceleration (optional)
docs.text:
AATM does not require a GPU. Local models (embedding functions and rerankers) run on the best device PyTorch can see: an NVIDIA GPU (CUDA), an Apple Silicon GPU (MPS), or the CPU. API-based models (OpenAI, Google) never use a local GPU.

You only need the NVIDIA driver, not the CUDA Toolkit: PyTorch's CUDA builds ship their own CUDA runtime.

docs.title: Check your setup with aatm doctor
docs.text:
aatm doctor

It reports your GPU, the highest CUDA version your driver supports (from nvidia-smi), the installed PyTorch build and the device AATM will use. When the GPU is not being used, it explains why and prints the commands that fix it, targeting the Python environment AATM is installed in. It never changes anything itself. It exits with code 1 when an action is needed, so it can be used in scripts.

docs.title: What pip install aatm gives you
docs.text:
PyTorch's default builds on PyPI differ by platform:

Platform Default PyTorch from PyPI GPU support Linux (x86_64) CUDA build (currently CUDA 13) Works if your driver supports that CUDA version Windows CPU-only build Install a CUDA build to use an NVIDIA GPU (below) macOS (Apple Silicon) Build with MPS Apple GPUs work out of the box

On Linux, run nvidia-smi: the top-right corner shows the highest CUDA version your driver supports. If it is older than the CUDA version of the default PyTorch build, update the driver or install a matching build as shown below. aatm doctor does this check for you.

docs.title: Installing a CUDA build of PyTorch manually
docs.text:
aatm doctor prints these commands with the right CUDA version filled in. To do it by hand, pick the CUDA version your driver supports (see nvidia-smi, or the PyTorch install selector).

Before installing AATM, install PyTorch first. pip then keeps that build:

pipuv 
pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128
pip install aatm

uv pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128
uv pip install aatm

If AATM is already installed, torch is already present, so a plain pip install torch --index-url ... does nothing. Replace it instead:

pipuv 
pip uninstall -y torch
pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128

uv pip install --reinstall-package torch torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128

On Linux machines without a GPU, you can avoid downloading several GB of CUDA libraries by installing the CPU-only build first:

pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu
pip install aatm

docs.title: Choosing the device
docs.text: When a local model loads, AATM logs the device it runs on. When it falls back to CPU, the log says why and suggests aatm doctor. Set AATM_DEVICE to cuda, mps or cpu to override the automatic choice (see Environment variables).

docs.title: Working from a clone of the repository
docs.text:
uv sync installs the CUDA 12.8 build of PyTorch on Linux and Windows. On a machine without an NVIDIA GPU, use the CPU-only build instead:

uv sync --no-group cu128 --group cpu

docs.title: From notes to OMOP tables
docs.text:
This page shows how to turn clinical notes into rows of OMOP CDM tables. You describe what to find in the notes and where each piece goes in the table; AATM extracts it with an LLM, codes it with the OMOP vocabularies and fills the rows as far as the notes allow.

Five tables are supported: measurement (scores, lab results), observation (smoking, family and medical history, and other facts), condition_occurrence (diagnoses, signs and symptoms), drug_exposure (drugs prescribed, given or taken) and device_exposure (implants, equipment and supplies).

If you have not extracted entities from a note before, read the Information extraction quick start first: this page builds on its entity definitions.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
1. Install AATM (Installation).
  2. Download the OMOP vocabularies from Athena. The predefined definitions on this page use SNOMED, LOINC and UCUM (units), so include at least those three.
  3. Run aatm init (CLI quick start). It builds the local vocabulary database (.aatm/omop.db), which every example on this page reads, and the search index the terminology mapper uses. Note the embedding model you choose (for example text-embedding-3-small): you pass the same name to the mapper later.
  4. Set an API key for the model provider, e.g. OPENAI_API_KEY (Environment variables).

Which definitions need what

Definition Table Needs the terminology mapper? ecog_performance_status measurement no smoking_status observation no lab_results measurement yes, to code test names family_history observation yes, to code conditions medical_history observation yes, to code conditions condition_occurrence condition_occurrence yes, to code conditions drug_exposure drug_exposure yes, to code drugs device_exposure device_exposure yes, to code devices

Definitions without the mapper only need the vocabulary database and an LLM, so they are the easiest way to start.

docs.title: Key terms
docs.text:
You do not need to know OMOP well to follow this page, but these words come up often.

Term Meaning CDM table A table of the OMOP Common Data Model, e.g. measurement. Each row is one fact about a patient. Concept An entry of the OMOP vocabularies, e.g. Body weight. Columns ending in _concept_id hold concept ids, numbers such as 3025315. Vocabulary and code Where a concept comes from and its code there, e.g. LOINC 29463-7. On this page codes are written LOINC:29463-7. Standard concept The concept OMOP uses for analysis when several mean the same thing. *_concept_id columns must hold standard concepts, from any vocabulary. A non-standard concept usually maps to a standard one. Domain The kind of concept: Measurement, Observation, Condition, Unit... Each column expects certain domains, e.g. measurement_concept_id takes Measurement concepts. Source value The text as written in the note, kept next to the code, e.g. measurement_source_value = "ECOG 4". 0 and NULL 0 means "there is a value, but it has no concept". Empty (NULL) means "nothing there".

docs.title: Your first run
docs.text:
This uses the predefined ECOG performance status definition, which needs no mapper.

ecog_to_omop.py
import asyncio

from aatm.omop import ClinicalNote, OmopExtractionPipeline

pipeline = OmopExtractionPipeline("ecog_performance_status", model_id="openai/gpt-5-mini")

notes = [
    ClinicalNote(
        text="Assessment 05/12/2025\nOncology follow-up. Bedbound, ECOG 4.",
        note_id=107,
        person_id=3,
        note_date="2025-06-01",
        visit_occurrence_id=507,
    ),
]

tables = asyncio.run(pipeline(notes))
measurement = tables["measurement"]
print(measurement.dropna(axis=1, how="all").to_string())  # only the filled columns

Scripts and notebooks

The pipeline is asynchronous. In a script, wrap the call in asyncio.run(...) as above. In a Jupyter notebook, write tables = await pipeline(notes) instead.

The table has every column of the CDM measurement table; dropna leaves out the empty ones when printing:

measurement_id person_id measurement_concept_id measurement_date measurement_type_concept_id value_as_number value_as_concept_id visit_occurrence_id measurement_source_value measurement_source_concept_id value_source_value 1 3 36305384 2025-05-12 32858 4.0 4174251 507 ECOG 4 4308014 4

docs.title: Reading the result
docs.text:
• measurement_id is generated, numbered from 1.
  • person_id and visit_occurrence_id come from the ClinicalNote, not from the text. They identify the patient and visit in your database, which the note cannot know.
  • measurement_concept_id 36305384 is the standard concept ECOG Performance Status score (LOINC 89247-1).
  • measurement_date is 2025-05-12, the assessment date written in the note. When a note gives no date, the note date (2025-06-01) is used instead.
  • measurement_type_concept_id 32858 means NLP: the row was derived from text.
  • value_as_number 4.0 and value_as_concept_id 4174251 (ECOG performance status - grade 4) are the grade, as a number and as a concept.
  • measurement_source_value and value_source_value keep what the note said.

ClinicalNote takes the note text and the values that come with the note: person_id, note_id, note_date, visit_occurrence_id, visit_detail_id and provider_id. All but text are optional; columns that need a missing value stay empty and are reported (see Issues). You can also pass plain strings instead of ClinicalNote objects.

docs.title: What you get back
docs.text:
pipeline(notes) returns an OmopTables object:

tables["measurement"]                                 # the rows, as a pandas DataFrame
tables.to_dataframes(provenance=True)["measurement"]  # plus where each row came from
tables.issues_dataframe()                             # what could not be filled, and why
tables.mappings_dataframe()                           # how extracted text was coded
tables.extraction_results                             # the extractor's raw output

With provenance=True, each row gets extra columns (_note_id, _entity_id, _text, _start, _end) pointing at the exact words of the note it was built from, so every row can be checked by a person.

docs.title: Issues
docs.text:
Rows are always returned, even when some columns could not be filled. Each gap is listed in tables.issues_dataframe(), with the row, the column, a reason and a detail.

Reason Meaning What to do missing_required A column the CDM requires is empty, e.g. person_id Pass it in the ClinicalNote unparsable_date A date is not a full date, e.g. "on admission". The next source (often the note date) was used Usually nothing; check the detail imputed_date_parts A date had no day or month, e.g. "March 2024", and was read as 2024-03-01 Decide if day-level precision matters unmapped_label The model chose a label that has no concept; 0 was stored Add the label to concepts, or accept 0 unmapped No standard concept was found for a text, e.g. the unit "lb"; 0 was stored Review in mappings_dataframe() low_confidence The mapper's score was below your min_score; 0 was stored Review the candidate in mappings_dataframe() domain_mismatch A coded concept is not of the domain the column expects Review the mapping invalid_value A value does not fit its column, e.g. text that is not a number Check the extracted text truncated A text was longer than its column (50 characters for *_source_value) Usually nothing multiple_children A mention had two children of the same kind, e.g. two dates; the first was used Check the note single_date The note gave only an end date, earlier than the fallback start date (often the note date); the end date was used for both, as the CDM allows Usually nothing

docs.title: Write your own: body weight, step by step
docs.text: This walkthrough builds a definition from scratch: body weight, stored in the measurement table with its unit. It needs no mapper.

docs.title: 1. Describe what to extract
docs.text:
An entity definition says what the model should find. Body weight has a value and a unit, so they are children of the weight mention (see Writing entity definitions):

body_weight.yaml
- name: Body weight
  key: body_weight
  definition: >
    The patient's measured body weight: the word for weight, the value and the unit,
    copied as written, e.g. "weight 72 kg" or "Wt: 158 lb". Stop at the unit: no
    words or punctuation after it. Does not include target or ideal weights, weight
    changes such as "lost 5 kg", or the weight of anyone other than the patient.

- name: Weight value
  key: weight_value
  definition: The number of a body weight, without the unit, e.g. "72" from "weight 72 kg".
  has_parent: true
  parent_key: body_weight

- name: Weight unit
  key: weight_unit
  definition: The unit of a body weight, copied as written without punctuation, e.g. "kg" or "lb".
  has_parent: true
  parent_key: body_weight

docs.title: 2. Say where each value goes
docs.text:
Add an omop block to the top-level entity. Each line names a column of the measurement table and where its value comes from:

body_weight.yaml (first entity)
- name: Body weight
  key: body_weight
  definition: >
    ...
  omop:
    table: measurement
    fields:
      person_id: {from: context.person_id}               # from the ClinicalNote
      measurement_concept_id: {concept: "LOINC:29463-7"}  # Body weight, always the same
      measurement_date: {from: context.note_date}
      measurement_type_concept_id: {value: 32858}         # NLP
      measurement_source_value: {from: text}              # the words of the mention
      value_as_number: {from: child.weight_value, as: float}
      unit_concept_id: {from: child.weight_unit, lookup: UCUM}  # "kg" -> kilogram
      unit_source_value: {from: child.weight_unit}

The omop block is never sent to the model: it only tells AATM how to fill the table. You can check what the model will read with definitions.to_prompt_str().

docs.title: 3. Check the codes before spending model calls
docs.text:
from aatm.data_models.extractors import EntityDefinitions
from aatm.omop import OmopTableBuilder

definitions = EntityDefinitions.from_yaml("body_weight.yaml")
OmopTableBuilder(definitions).describe_concepts()
entity column label code concept_id concept_name vocabulary_id domain_id body_weight measurement_concept_id LOINC:29463-7 3025315 Body weight LOINC Measurement

Loading the file and creating the builder already check a lot: unknown columns, typos in child. or attribute. names, codes missing from the vocabulary, and non-standard concepts all fail here, with a message saying what is wrong (see Troubleshooting).

docs.title: 4. Run it
docs.text:
import asyncio

from aatm.omop import ClinicalNote, OmopExtractionPipeline

notes = [
    ClinicalNote(text="Weight 72 kg today. Goal weight 65 kg.", person_id=1, note_date="2025-06-01"),
    ClinicalNote(text="Wt: 158 lb. Lost 5 lb since March.", person_id=2, note_date="2025-06-02"),
]

pipeline = OmopExtractionPipeline(definitions, model_id="openai/gpt-5-mini")
tables = asyncio.run(pipeline(notes))
tables["measurement"]
measurement_id person_id measurement_concept_id measurement_date measurement_type_concept_id value_as_number unit_concept_id measurement_source_value unit_source_value 1 1 3025315 2025-06-01 32858 72.0 9529 Weight 72 kg kg 2 2 3025315 2025-06-02 32858 158.0 0 Wt: 158 lb lb

The goal weight and the weight loss were left out, as the definition asks.

docs.title: 5. Read the issues
docs.text:
tables.issues_dataframe()
row_id column reason detail 2 unit_concept_id unmapped No concept for 'lb' with a UCUM code lookup; stored 0

"kg" is a UCUM code, so it was found (kilogram, 9529). "lb" is not: UCUM writes pounds as [lb_av]. The row is kept with unit_concept_id = 0, which the CDM uses for "there is a unit, but it is not mapped", and unit_source_value keeps "lb".

Iterate on real notes

Most fixes are in the wording of the definitions. The first version of this example said only "copied as written", and the model returned "Weight 72 kg today." and "lb.". Adding "Stop at the unit: no words or punctuation after it" fixed both.

docs.title: Column sources
docs.text:
Each column has one source:

Source Value Example {from: text} The words of the mention "ECOG 4" {from: attribute.<key>} The label the model chose for an attribute "4" {from: child.<key>} The text of the mention's child with that key "05/12/2025" {from: context.<name>} A field of the ClinicalNote person_id {value: <constant>} A fixed value 32858 {concept: "<VOCABULARY>:<code>"} The concept id of a code "LOINC:29463-7"

A list of sources is tried in order, and the first that gives a value wins. The ECOG definition uses this for the date: the assessment date if the note states a full one, else the note date:

      measurement_date:
        - {from: child.assessment_date, as: date}
        - {from: context.note_date}

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Option Use with Effect as: int, float, str or date from: Convert the text. Dates are read from text such as "05/12/2025" or "March 2024"; decimal commas ("11,2") are accepted as: days from: Read a duration as a number of days: "7 days", "x7d", "2 weeks", "1 month" (30 days), "14 dias" period_start: <column> as: days, or an integer value: Store the last day of a period of N days starting on that column's date: the date + N - 1. The column must be mapped before this one when: {attribute.<key>: [<label>, ...]} any source Use the source only when the attribute has one of these labels; otherwise try the next source concepts: {<label>: "<VOCABULARY>:<code>"} from: attribute.<key> Store the concept of the chosen label instead of the label maps_to: true concept: or concepts: Store the standard concept the code maps to lookup: <VOCABULARY> from: Find the text as a code of that vocabulary, e.g. units in UCUM map: {...} from: Code the text with the terminology mapper (see below)

The table's id column (measurement_id, observation_id) is generated, numbered from id_start (default 1). Only top-level entities can have an omop block; a child's text is used from its parent with from: child.<key>.

docs.title: Fixed codes, standard concepts and domains
docs.text:
Write codes as VOCABULARY:code, as they appear in the vocabulary, rather than as concept ids, so the file stays readable. They are looked up when the builder is created, and these fail before any model call:

  • a code that is not in the vocabulary;
  • a non-standard concept in a *_concept_id column. Add maps_to: true to use the standard concept it maps to;
  • a concept of a domain the column does not accept, e.g. a Condition concept in measurement_concept_id;
  • maps_to: true on a code without exactly one standard mapping.

*_source_concept_id columns keep the code as written, standard or not, as the CDM asks. The ECOG definition shows why both exist:

      measurement_concept_id: {concept: "SNOMED:423740007", maps_to: true}
      measurement_source_concept_id: {concept: "SNOMED:423740007"}

SNOMED 423740007 ECOG performance status is not standard; it maps to LOINC 89247-1 ECOG Performance Status score, which goes to measurement_concept_id, while the SNOMED concept is kept in measurement_source_concept_id.

Standard, from any vocabulary

A *_concept_id column needs a standard concept of the right domain. Its vocabulary does not matter: SNOMED, LOINC, RxNorm or any other. The rule applies to every source: fixed codes and label maps are checked when the builder is created, and a map or lookup that finds only a non-standard concept stores 0 and reports unmapped.

docs.title: Coding text with the terminology mapper
docs.text:
Some concepts never change (body weight is always Body weight), but many depend on what the note says: the name of a lab test, a condition. A map source sends the extracted text to the same TerminologyMapper used for terminology mapping, which searches the vocabularies and picks the best standard concept.

The predefined lab_results definition codes the test name this way:

      measurement_concept_id:
        from: text
        map: {}          # any standard concept of the column's domain (Measurement)

The YAML says what to code. Your code chooses how, by configuring the mapper, because that involves search models, LLMs and API keys:

import asyncio

from aatm.omop import ClinicalNote, OmopExtractionPipeline
from aatm.selectors import OpenAILLMSelector
from aatm.terminology_mapper import TerminologyMapper

mapper = TerminologyMapper(
    retriever="text-embedding-3-small",          # the embedding model chosen in `aatm init`
    selector=OpenAILLMSelector("gpt-5-mini"),    # an LLM picks among the candidates
)
mapper.retriever.top_k = 30                      # how many candidates it sees

pipeline = OmopExtractionPipeline("lab_results", model_id="openai/gpt-5-mini", mapper=mapper)
notes = [ClinicalNote(text="Labs 03/15/2025: Hb 11.2 g/dL, creatinine 1.4 mg/dl.", person_id=10)]
tables = asyncio.run(pipeline(notes))
tables.mappings_dataframe()

mappings_dataframe() has one row per coded text, so you can review every choice:

row_id column text method concept_id concept_name score stored 1 measurement_concept_id Hb map 3000963 Hemoglobin [Mass/volume] in Blood 0.30 3000963 1 unit_concept_id g/dL lookup 8713 gram per deciliter 8713

How it works:

  • The search is limited to a domain, not a vocabulary. By default it is the domain the column requires (Measurement here). map: {domain: Condition} sets it explicitly, and map: {vocabularies: [LOINC]} narrows the search further if your data must use one vocabulary.
  • Each distinct text is coded once per run: a hundred notes mentioning "Hb" make one mapper query.
  • min_score (map: {min_score: 0.8}) stores 0 and reports low_confidence below that score. Scores depend on the retriever, so look at real scores in mappings_dataframe() before choosing a threshold.

Review the mappings

Short names are ambiguous. In a small test with nine lab results, the default selector, which takes the closest match, coded only 2 test names correctly; with OpenAILLMSelector choosing among 30 candidates, 7 of 9 were correct. Without a vocabulary filter, some tests map to general SNOMED procedures such as Potassium measurement rather than the more specific LOINC Potassium [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma; both are valid standard concepts.

docs.title: Code lookups
docs.text: lookup: <VOCABULARY> finds the extracted text as a code of a vocabulary. It suits units: "g/dL" is the UCUM code of gram per deciliter. An exact match wins; otherwise a single standard concept matching while ignoring case is used ("mg/dl" → mg/dL). Texts that are not codes, such as "lb" or "x10^3/uL", are reported as unmapped.

docs.title: The observation table
docs.text:
The observation table holds facts that are not measurements, conditions, procedures, drugs or devices: smoking, family history, social and lifestyle facts. Each row pairs an observation_concept_id (what was observed) with a value: a concept, a number, a text or a date.

Several definitions can run together, so each note is sent to the model only once:

import asyncio

from aatm.omop import ClinicalNote, OmopExtractionPipeline
from aatm.selectors import OpenAILLMSelector
from aatm.terminology_mapper import TerminologyMapper

mapper = TerminologyMapper(retriever="text-embedding-3-small", selector=OpenAILLMSelector("gpt-5-mini"))
mapper.retriever.top_k = 30

pipeline = OmopExtractionPipeline(
    ["smoking_status", "family_history", "medical_history"],  # names, YAML paths, or both
    model_id="openai/gpt-5-mini",
    mapper=mapper,  # family_history and medical_history code conditions with it
)
notes = [
    ClinicalNote(
        text=(
            "Former smoker, 30 pack-years. Mother had breast cancer at 45. "
            "History of appendicitis."
        ),
        person_id=20,
        note_date="2025-06-01",
    ),
]
tables = asyncio.run(pipeline(notes))
tables["observation"]

A typical result (concept names added in italics):

observation_id observation_concept_id observation_source_value value_as_number value_as_concept_id value_source_value qualifier_concept_id unit_concept_id 1 43054909 Tobacco smoking status Former smoker 45883458 Former smoker former 2 3003421 Cigarettes smoked total (pack per year) 30 pack-years 30.0 30 0 3 4167217 Family history of clinical finding breast cancer 4112853 Malignant tumor of breast breast cancer 4248584 Mother 4 3002660 History of Past illness Narrative appendicitis 440448 Appendicitis appendicitis

smoking_status gives up to two rows per mention:

  • Smoking status, with the status as a concept in value_as_concept_id: never, former, current every day, current some day, or current without a frequency. "Non-smoker" or "denies smoking" do not say whether the patient ever smoked, so they get the label not_current, stored as 0 and reported as unmapped_label.
  • Pack-years, with the number in value_as_number. UCUM has no code for pack-years, so unit_concept_id is 0 and unit_source_value is "pack-years".

family_history follows the CDM convention for family history: observation_concept_id is Family history of clinical finding, value_as_concept_id is the condition, coded by the mapper, and qualifier_concept_id is the relative (Mother, Sister...). The CDM has no column for the relative, so that last choice is a convention of this definition; qualifier_source_value keeps the label.

medical_history takes the patient's past conditions, which the CDM keeps out of condition_occurrence: "history of appendicitis", "h/o stroke, no sequelae", "hepatitis C, treated and cured". observation_concept_id is LOINC 11348-0 History of Past illness Narrative and value_as_concept_id is the condition, coded by the mapper, as for family history. Conditions the patient still has, even when listed under past medical history ("PMH: hypertension"), go to condition_occurrence, and past surgeries ("s/p appendectomy") are not extracted. When the past condition happened is not captured: observation_date is the note date.

Why LOINC 11348-0

SNOMED History of clinical finding in subject is not a standard concept. The vocabulary maps precoordinated SNOMED concepts such as History of myocardial infarction to the condition with Maps to value. Their Maps to target is in the OMOP Extension vocabulary, which the other predefined definitions do not need. To use a different concept, copy medical_history.yaml and change observation_concept_id.

Which concepts the observation table accepts

The CDM sends Condition, Procedure, Drug, Measurement, Device and Specimen concepts to their own tables, so observation_concept_id rejects them. value_as_concept_id accepts any domain: for family history it holds a condition.

When you combine definitions, every entity key must be unique. A clash fails with a message naming the files:

Entity keys must be unique across the combined definitions, since the model's output is matched to definitions by key:
  - key 'smoking_status' is defined in predefined 'smoking_status' and definitions/alcohol_use.yaml
List each file once, and rename keys that clash in your own files.

docs.title: The condition_occurrence table
docs.text:
The condition_occurrence table holds the patient's diagnoses, problems, signs and symptoms. Each row is one mention of a condition, with its standard concept, its dates and a status.

import asyncio

from aatm.omop import ClinicalNote, OmopExtractionPipeline
from aatm.selectors import OpenAILLMSelector
from aatm.terminology_mapper import TerminologyMapper

mapper = TerminologyMapper(retriever="text-embedding-3-small", selector=OpenAILLMSelector("gpt-5-mini"))
mapper.retriever.top_k = 30

pipeline = OmopExtractionPipeline(
    "condition_occurrence",
    model_id="openai/gpt-5-mini",
    mapper=mapper,  # codes condition names
)
notes = [
    ClinicalNote(
        text=(
            "Type 2 diabetes since 2019. Probable community-acquired pneumonia. "
            "History of appendicitis. Rule out PE. Denies chest pain. "
            "Mother had breast cancer."
        ),
        person_id=20,
        note_date="2025-06-01",
    ),
]
tables = asyncio.run(pipeline(notes))
tables["condition_occurrence"]

A run with gpt-5-mini gave two rows (concept names added in italics):

condition_occurrence_id condition_concept_id condition_source_value condition_start_date condition_status_concept_id condition_status_source_value condition_type_concept_id 1 201826 Type 2 diabetes mellitus Type 2 diabetes 2019-01-01 32893 Confirmed diagnosis confirmed 32858 NLP 2 4293463 Community acquired pneumonia community-acquired pneumonia 2025-06-01 32899 Preliminary diagnosis preliminary 32858 NLP

The only issue is imputed_date_parts on row 1: "2019" has no month or day and is read as 2019-01-01.

What is not a row. The definition follows the CDM conventions for this table, so the other four conditions of the note are left out:

In the note Why it is not here "History of appendicitis" Past diagnoses belong in observation, says the CDM: add medical_history to the list of definitions to keep it. Long-standing conditions the patient still has, e.g. "PMH: hypertension", are kept. "Rule out PE" Rule-out and "question of" diagnoses are not recorded in this table. "Denies chest pain" Negated. "Mother had breast cancer" Family history belongs in observation: add family_history to the list of definitions to keep it.

Status. Each condition gets a required status label, stored in condition_status_concept_id:

Label Means Concept confirmed Stated as a fact, e.g. "hypertension", "diagnosed with asthma in 2010" 32893 Confirmed diagnosis preliminary A likely working diagnosis, e.g. "probable pneumonia", "presumed sepsis" 32899 Preliminary diagnosis

The CDM's own examples of a status are the point in the visit when the diagnosis was given (admitting, principal, secondary diagnosis). Notes rarely say that, so it is not extracted.

Dates. condition_start_date is the first that applies:

  1. the start date the note gives for that condition ("since 2019" → 2019-01-01, reported as imputed_date_parts);
  2. the note date. The condition is known to be present then, but may have started much earlier, so read these start dates as "recorded on" rather than "onset".

When the note gives only an end date before the note date ("pneumonia, resolved 2024-04-10"), that date is used for both start and end, as the CDM allows for a single date, and reported as single_date.

The CDM notes that most sources have no condition start date, and records most conditions as snapshots without an end date. condition_end_date is the end date the note gives, e.g. for an episode in a discharge summary ("pneumonia from 03/01/2025 to 03/10/2025"). An end date before the start date is left empty and reported as invalid_value.

Which concepts the condition_occurrence table accepts

condition_concept_id takes standard concepts of the Condition domain only. The mapper searches that domain, and a concept of another domain, e.g. a procedure, is stored but reported as domain_mismatch. Check the coded conditions with tables.mappings_dataframe().

docs.title: The drug_exposure table
docs.text:
The drug_exposure table holds the drugs a patient is prescribed, is given or takes: medicines, vaccines and biologics. Each row is one mention of a drug, with its standard concept, its dates, the route and the dosing instructions. The predefined definition follows the CDM conventions for this table and the THEMIS conventions for drug_exposure.

import asyncio

from aatm.omop import ClinicalNote, OmopExtractionPipeline
from aatm.selectors import OpenAILLMSelector
from aatm.terminology_mapper import TerminologyMapper

mapper = TerminologyMapper(retriever="text-embedding-3-small", selector=OpenAILLMSelector("gpt-5-mini"))
mapper.retriever.top_k = 30

pipeline = OmopExtractionPipeline(
    "drug_exposure",
    model_id="openai/gpt-5-mini",
    mapper=mapper,  # codes drug names
)
notes = [
    ClinicalNote(
        text=(
            "Home meds: lisinopril 10 mg PO daily since 2020, metformin 500 mg tablet BID.\n"
            "Ceftriaxone 1 g IV given in the ED.\n"
            "Plan: start amoxicillin 875 mg PO BID for 7 days. Consider a statin.\n"
            "Allergic to penicillin. Not on anticoagulation."
        ),
        person_id=30,
        note_date="2025-06-01",
        visit_occurrence_id=900,
        provider_id=12,
    ),
]
tables = asyncio.run(pipeline(notes))
tables["drug_exposure"]

A run with gpt-5-mini gave four rows (concept names added in italics; drug_type_concept_id is 32858 NLP in every row):

drug_exposure_id drug_concept_id drug_source_value start end route_concept_id sig visit_occurrence_id provider_id 1 1308304 lisinopril 10 MG lisinopril 10 mg 2020-01-01 2025-06-01 4132161 Oral 2 40164929 metformin hydrochloride 500 MG Oral Tablet metformin 500 mg tablet 2025-06-01 2025-06-01 3 46287328 ceftriaxone 1000 MG Injection Ceftriaxone 1 g 2025-06-01 2025-06-01 4171047 Intravenous 900 12 4 19083494 amoxicillin 875 MG amoxicillin 875 mg 2025-06-01 2025-06-07 4132161 Oral 875 mg PO BID for 7 days 900 12

"Consider a statin" is only considered, the penicillin is an allergy and anticoagulation is negated, so none of them is a row. Drug classes such as "antihypertensives" are left out too: the CDM would store them with drug_concept_id = 0.

Kind. Each drug gets a required kind label, which decides the end date and the visit:

Label Means Visit and provider administered Given to the patient, e.g. "ceftriaxone 1 g IV given in the ED" From the note prescribed Started, prescribed or changed in this note, e.g. "start amoxicillin" From the note taking On the patient's medication list, or reported use Left empty: the CDM fills the visit only when the exposure was started in it

Dates. drug_exposure_start_date is the start date the note gives, else the note date. drug_exposure_end_date is required by the CDM; when the note gives none, it is inferred as THEMIS ratified:

  1. the end date the note gives ("until 06/10/2025"), also kept in verbatim_end_date;
  2. the start date + the planned duration - 1 day ("for 7 days" → 2025-06-07);
  3. for a prescribed drug, the start date + 29 days;
  4. for a taking drug, the note date: the last date it is known to be taken. THEMIS has no rule for medication lists, so this is a convention of this definition;
  5. for an administered drug, the start date.

When the note gives only a stop date before the note date ("aspirin stopped on 05/01/2025"), that date is used for both start and end and reported as single_date, rather than a start after the stop.

Route. The optional route label (oral, intravenous, subcutaneous, inhaled, ...) is stored as its standard SNOMED route concept in route_concept_id.

Not filled. The CDM fills days_supply only from a verbatim days supply, never from other fields, so a duration in a note does not go there. quantity, refills, stop_reason and lot_number are left empty, and dose_unit_source_value is a legacy column the CDM plans to deprecate.

Check the coded drugs

drug_concept_id takes standard concepts of the Drug domain. The CDM prefers the most detailed concept the source supports, such as a clinical drug, over an ingredient, so the mention keeps the strength and dose form. A name without detail can be coded too specifically: in one run "Influenza vaccine" was coded as one seasonal formulation, with a score of 0.41. Review low scores with tables.mappings_dataframe().

docs.title: The device_exposure table
docs.text:
The device_exposure table holds the medical devices a patient has or is given: implants (pacemakers, stents, artificial joints), equipment and supplies (crutches, catheters, insulin pumps, CPAP) and materials such as sutures. Each row is one mention of a device, with its standard concept, its dates and the number of devices. The predefined definition follows the CDM conventions for this table; THEMIS has no device conventions.

import asyncio

from aatm.omop import ClinicalNote, OmopExtractionPipeline
from aatm.selectors import OpenAILLMSelector
from aatm.terminology_mapper import TerminologyMapper

mapper = TerminologyMapper(retriever="text-embedding-3-small", selector=OpenAILLMSelector("gpt-5-mini"))
mapper.retriever.top_k = 30

pipeline = OmopExtractionPipeline(
    "device_exposure",
    model_id="openai/gpt-5-mini",
    mapper=mapper,  # codes device names
)
notes = [
    ClinicalNote(
        text=(
            "s/p PCI with 2 drug-eluting stents in 2021. Dual-chamber pacemaker since 2019.\n"
            "Foley catheter inserted today for retention. Walks with crutches.\n"
            "No indwelling lines. Candidate for ICD. Nicotine patch 21 mg daily."
        ),
        person_id=40,
        note_date="2025-06-01",
        visit_occurrence_id=950,
        provider_id=14,
    ),
]
tables = asyncio.run(pipeline(notes))
tables["device_exposure"]

A run with gpt-5-mini gave four rows (concept names added in italics; device_type_concept_id is 32858 NLP in every row):

device_exposure_id device_concept_id device_source_value start end quantity visit_occurrence_id provider_id 1 4131681 Drug eluting stent drug-eluting stents 2021-01-01 2 2 40481477 Dual chamber pulse generator, device Dual-chamber pacemaker 2019-01-01 1 3 40625746 Foley catheter Foley catheter 2025-06-01 1 950 14 4 4251933 Crutch crutches 2025-06-01 1

The PCI is a procedure, the action of placing the stents: only the stents are a device. "No indwelling lines" is negated, the ICD is only considered, and the nicotine patch is a drug, which belongs in drug_exposure. So none of them is a row.

Kind. Each device gets a required kind label:

Label Means Visit and provider placed Implanted, inserted, applied, prescribed or supplied in this encounter, e.g. "Foley catheter inserted today" From the note existing The patient already has or uses it, e.g. "has a pacemaker", "walks with crutches" Left empty: the CDM fills the visit only when the exposure was started in it

Dates. device_exposure_start_date is the date the note gives (e.g. the implant date, "since 2019" → 2019-01-01, reported as imputed_date_parts), else the note date. Unlike drug_exposure, the end date is optional, and the CDM fills it only when the source gives it, so it is never inferred. When the note gives only a removal date ("PICC line removed on 05/20/2025"), it is used for both dates and reported as single_date.

Quantity. The number the note gives ("2 drug-eluting stents"), else 1: the CDM stores 1 when a device exposure exists without a quantity.

Not filled. unique_device_id and production_id (the UDI, rarely written in notes), the unit columns, which the CDM leaves NULL when the source has no unit, and the datetime columns.

Check the coded devices

device_concept_id takes standard concepts of the Device domain. Device names in notes are often short ("CPAP", "brace"), and mapper scores were low even for right answers in our runs, e.g. "left knee brace" → Knee orthosis at 0.31. Review them with tables.mappings_dataframe() before setting a min_score.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: You see Why Fix OMOP vocabulary database not found: .aatm/omop.db. Run aatm init to build it. The vocabulary database is missing, or the script runs from another folder Run aatm init, or pass vocabulary="path/to/omop.db" Concepts not found in the vocabulary: ['LOINC:29463-8'] A typo in a code, or that vocabulary was not downloaded from Athena Check the code on Athena and that its vocabulary was included in aatm init ... is not a standard concept. Add 'maps_to: true' to use the standard concept it maps to A *_concept_id column got a non-standard code Add maps_to: true, or use the standard concept's code Table 'measurement' has no column 'value_as_numbr' A typo in a column name Use the column names of the CDM table 'weight_val' is not a child entity of 'body_weight' from: child.<key> names an entity that is not a child of this one Use the child's key, and check its parent_key ... uses 'map', so the builder needs a terminology mapper The definition codes text, but no mapper was given Pass mapper=TerminologyMapper(...) SyntaxError: 'await' outside function await used in a script Use asyncio.run(pipeline(notes)), or run it in a notebook Every map is unmapped The mapper found no candidates, e.g. the search index for its retriever was not built Use the embedding model you chose in aatm init as the retriever

docs.title: Current limits
docs.text:
• Only the measurement, observation, condition_occurrence, drug_exposure and device_exposure tables are supported so far.
  • drug_exposure end dates are not inferred from the quantity and daily dose (the second THEMIS rule), and mail-order prescriptions are not told apart from others.
  • condition_start_date falls back to the note date when the note gives no date, which is later than the real onset of long-standing conditions.
  • map searches with the extracted text alone: a unit such as mg/dL, which hints at a serum test, is not used.
  • Mapper scores are not comparable across retrievers and selectors.
  • Units written outside UCUM ("lb", "x10^3/uL", "mEq/L") are not converted before the lookup.
  • Relative dates ("on admission", "after cycle 2") are not resolved: the next source, usually the note date, is used and the issue is reported.

docs.title: CLI Quick Start
docs.text:
This page shows how to use AATM entirely from the command line.

It is focused on the actual CLI workflow exposed by the commads: init, map, and search-ui.

docs.title: What you can do from the CLI
docs.text:
With the CLI, you can:

  • initialize the local environment
  • build the local SQLite vocabulary database
  • build the mapping datasets
  • build the local vector database
  • run terminology mapping jobs
  • launch the interactive search UI

The main commands are:

  • aatm init
  • aatm map
  • aatm search-ui

docs.title: 1. Prepare your OMOP vocabularies directory
docs.text:
Before running aatm init, download the OMOP vocabularies you want to use and place them in a directory. You can find them at https://athena.ohdsi.org/vocabulary/list

By default, the CLI expects it at the root directory:

./vocabularies

If you do not use that location, you can point the CLI to a different directory with the option --vocab-dir or -vd. The CLI validates this path during initialization.

docs.title: 2. Run the initialization command
docs.text:
The init command is the main CLI setup workflow.

It does all of the following for you:

  • creates the local .aatm helper directory where the local databases and aatm config files will be stored
  • ensures .aatm is added to .gitignore
  • builds the local OMOP SQLite database
  • lets you choose an embedding model
  • lets you choose the standard vocabularies
  • builds the mapping datasets
  • builds the local vector database

That means you do not need to call Python setup functions manually for the normal setup flow. At the end, you will be ready to run terminology mapping tasks.

docs.title: Simplest setup
docs.text:
aatm init

This uses the default vocab directory and interactively asks you to choose the embedding model, standard vocabularies and other options.

docs.title: Setup with a custom vocab directory
docs.text: aatm init --vocab-dir ./my_vocabularies

docs.title: Setup with an explicit embedding model
docs.text: aatm init --embedding-model embeddinggemma-300M

docs.title: Setup with explicit standard vocabularies
docs.text: aatm init --standard-vocabs LOINC --standard-vocabs SNOMED --standard-vocabs RxNorm

docs.title: Fully explicit setup
docs.text:
aatm init \
  --vocab-dir ./vocabularies \
  --embedding-model embeddinggemma-300M \
  --standard-vocabs LOINC \
  --standard-vocabs SNOMED \
  --standard-vocabs RxNorm

docs.title: 3. Prepare your input CSV
docs.text:
After initialization, prepare the CSV you want to map.

The mapper expects an OMOP-style SOURCE_TO_CONCEPT_MAP input structure, including these columns:

  • source_code
  • source_concept_id
  • source_vocabulary_id
  • source_code_description
  • valid_start_date
  • valid_end_date
  • invalid_reason

Example:

source_code,source_concept_id,source_vocabulary_id,source_code_description,valid_start_date,valid_end_date,invalid_reason
A01,,LOCAL,"Dor no peito",2020-01-01,2099-12-31,
B02,,LOCAL,"Diabetes mellitus tipo 2",2020-01-01,2099-12-31,

docs.title: 4. Run mapping directly from the CLI
docs.text:
The map command runs a terminology mapping task. You can use it in two ways:

  • with a task config file
  • with explicit CLI options

Both paths are supported directly by the CLI implementation.

docs.title: Option A: run from explicit CLI arguments
docs.text:
This is the most direct fully-CLI workflow.

aatm map \
  --input-file data/source_to_concept_map.csv \
  --output-dir output \
  --translator-id empty-translator \
  --retriever-id embeddinggemma-300M \
  --reranker-id bm25-reranker \
  --selector-id first-result-selector \
  --batch-size 100

docs.title: Run a small test job
docs.text:
Use --limit-to when you want to test with only a few rows.

aatm map \
  --input-file data/source_to_concept_map.csv \
  --output-dir output \
  --translator-id empty-translator \
  --retriever-id embeddinggemma-300M \
  --reranker-id bm25-reranker \
  --selector-id first-result-selector \
  --limit-to 20

docs.title: Apply rate limiting
docs.text:
If needed, you can also pass a rate limit:

aatm map \
  --input-file data/source_to_concept_map.csv \
  --output-dir output \
  --translator-id gemini-2.5-flash \
  --retriever-id embeddinggemma-300M \
  --reranker-id bm25-reranker \
  --selector-id first-result-selector \
  --batch-size 50 \
  --rate-limit 100

The CLI accepts all of these options directly.

docs.title: Option B. Run mapping from a config file
docs.text: The other CLI workflow is to store the mapping task in a config file and pass it with --task-config-path or -t.

docs.title: Example command
docs.text:
aatm map --task-config-path task.yaml

When you do this, the CLI loads the task config file and runs the mapping task from it.

docs.title: Example task config
docs.text:
Task config files are supported as .yaml or .json files.

YAMLJSON 
input_file: data/source_to_concept_map.csv
output_dir: output
translator_id: empty-translator
retriever_id: embeddinggemma-300M
reranker_id: bm25-reranker
selector_id: first-result-selector
batch_size: 100
rate_limit: null
limit_to: null

{
  "input_file": "data/source_to_concept_map.csv",
  "output_dir": "output",
  "translator_id": "empty-translator",
  "retriever_id": "embeddinggemma-300M",
  "reranker_id": "bm25-reranker",
  "selector_id": "first-result-selector",
  "batch_size": 100,
  "rate_limit": null,
  "limit_to": null
}

This is useful when you want reproducible runs or reusable task definitions.

docs.title: 5. Launch the search UI from the CLI
docs.text:
You can also launch the Streamlit-based search interface directly from the CLI:

aatm search-ui

The CLI resolves the packaged search_ui.py file and launches it through Streamlit using the current Python interpreter. Streamlit's file watcher is turned off, since it is only needed while editing the UI; set STREAMLIT_SERVER_FILE_WATCHER_TYPE=auto to turn it back on.

Streamlit search UI screenshot.

docs.title: 6. What gets created locally
docs.text:
After a normal CLI setup and mapping workflow, you will typically have local artifacts such as:

.aatm/
├── omop.db
├── datasets/
└── chroma_vector_dbs/

And your mapped output will typically be written to:

output/mapped_source_concepts.csv

The CLI init command is responsible for creating the local helper resources, and the map command runs the terminology mapping workflow.

docs.title: 7. End-to-end CLI example
docs.text: Here is a full CLI-only path.

docs.title: Step 1: initialize
docs.text:
aatm init \
  --vocab-dir ./vocabularies \
  --embedding-model embeddinggemma-300M \
  --standard-vocabs LOINC \
  --standard-vocabs SNOMED \
  --standard-vocabs RxNorm

docs.title: Step 2: run mapping
docs.text:
aatm map \
  --input-file data/source_to_concept_map.csv \
  --output-dir output \
  --translator-id empty-translator \
  --retriever-id embeddinggemma-300M \
  --reranker-id bm25-reranker \
  --selector-id first-result-selector \
  --batch-size 100

docs.title: Step 3: inspect output
docs.text:
ls output

You should see the mapped CSV file there.

docs.title: Step 4: optionally launch the search UI
docs.text: aatm search-ui

docs.title: aatm init says the vocabulary directory does not exist
docs.text:
Make sure your OMOP vocabulary files are present in ./vocabularies, or pass the correct path with:

aatm init --vocab-dir /path/to/vocabularies

The CLI explicitly checks whether the provided directory exists.

docs.title: aatm init says the embedding model is unsupported
docs.text: Use one of the supported model names listed in this page. The CLI validates the model name before continuing.

docs.title: aatm map says the task config file does not exist
docs.text:
Check the path you passed to:

aatm map --task-config-path task.yaml

The CLI verifies that the config file exists before loading it.

docs.title: Retrieval fails at mapping time
docs.text: Make sure you ran aatm init first and successfully built the local vector database for the retriever you want to use.

docs.title: API-backed components fail
docs.text: Check that your .env file contains the required API keys.

docs.title: Seeing more (or fewer) log messages
docs.text:
Every command accepts a global --log-level option (or -l), placed before the command name. Logs are written to stderr:

aatm --log-level DEBUG map --task-config-path task.yaml

The level can also be set with the AATM_LOG_LEVEL environment variable. It is passed on to aatm serve and aatm search-ui.

docs.title: Output redirected to a file looks garbled or fails
docs.text: The CLI writes UTF-8 to files and pipes (for example aatm serve > server.log), so open such files as UTF-8.

docs.title: Information Extraction Quick Start
docs.text: This page shows how to extract structured information, such as conditions, drugs and their dates, from clinical documents with the AATM information extraction pipeline.

docs.title: What the pipeline does
docs.text:
Given a clinical note and a set of entity definitions (what to extract), the pipeline asks an LLM to find every relevant mention and then validates the answer against the note. Only spans that really exist in the note survive, each with its exact character position, linked to the entity it belongs to.

flowchart LR
    A[Clinical note] --> B[Numbered lines]
    D[Entity definitions] --> C
    B --> C[LLM extraction]
    C --> E[Validation]
    E --> F[Validated entities<br/>+ rejected candidates]
    F --> G[Records view]

The main pieces are:

Piece Where Role EntityDefinitions aatm.data_models.extractors Which entities to extract, loaded from YAML SimpleLLMExtractor aatm.extractors Sends each note to the LLM and validates the output validate_extracted_entity aatm.data_models.extractors Grounds and checks the model output (also usable on its own) EntityValidationResult aatm.data_models.extractors Validated entities, rejected candidates and the records view

The extracted text (for example "Hypertension" or "Furosemide 40 mg") can then be mapped to standard concepts with the terminology mapping pipeline.

docs.title: 1. Requirements
docs.text:
• A model that supports structured outputs, from one of the providers below. Model ids are prefixed with the provider: <provider>/<model name>.
  • The provider's API key in its environment variable (see Environment variables), or passed with api_key=....
Provider model_id example Key Notes OpenAI openai/gpt-5 OPENAI_API_KEY Google Gemini gemini/gemini-3-flash-preview GOOGLE_API_KEY Anthropic anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 ANTHROPIC_API_KEY Install with pip install "aatm[anthropic]" Ollama ollama/llama3.3 none Uses http://localhost:11434/v1 unless base_url is given OpenRouter openrouter/qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b OPENROUTER_API_KEY Any OpenAI-compatible server (vLLM, LM Studio, Together, ...) openai-compatible/<model> api_key=... if needed Requires base_url=... 
extractor = SimpleLLMExtractor(
    model_id="openai-compatible/Qwen/Qwen3-32B",
    base_url="http://localhost:8000/v1",  # e.g. a local vLLM server
    entity_definitions=entity_definitions,
)

Other providers can be added with aatm.llm.register_provider, or by passing any object with an async generate(system=..., user=..., output_type=...) method as llm=....

docs.title: 2. A first extraction
docs.text:
from aatm.data_models.extractors import EntityDefinitions
from aatm.extractors import SimpleLLMExtractor

entity_definitions = EntityDefinitions.from_predefined("condition_occurrence")

extractor = SimpleLLMExtractor(
